verdict: SHIP, scoped. Reused Q023's spike unchanged; swept 5 edit positions x 4 N values (20 runs). editOne cost is a clean linear function of compilation-order successors at every N, and the per-successor slope shows no detectable systematic drift from N=10 to N=300 (peak slope lands at a middle N in both the executor's and the independent reviewer's data, refuting the pre-registered REVISE trigger). KILL never fired. Scoped down by review: 'slope is essentially N-invariant' overstates what 5 points per fit can support (95% CI is +/-76% at N=10, only N=150/300 are tight - correct claim is 'no detectable drift', not 'proven invariant'); the 'intercept tracks repeat median' cross-validation is mildly circular since the zero-successor point is inside the regression; one N=50 data point (succ=25 approx succ=12) was a sampling outlier that did not reproduce. Most importantly: this is a cost model (whole-project ParseAndCheckProject, independent files) generalizing across N, not a measured FSAC live-editing session cost - must not be cited as 'FSAC keystroke cost characterized', and Myriad's real attributed types tend to sit early in build order, near the expensive end of this curve.
